# docs.airbyte.com llms.txt

> Airbyte is an open source platform designed for building and managing data pipelines, offering extensive connector options to facilitate data movement from various sources to destinations efficiently and effectively.

- [docs.airbyte.com llms.txt](https://docs.airbyte.io/index.md)

## search

- [Search the documentation](https://docs.airbyte.io/search.md)

## ai-agents

Airbyte Agents is a data and context layer for AI agents. It gives your agents real-time access to business data through open source, type-safe connectors, managed credentials, and low-latency search. Use it as a cloud platform or import connectors directly into your own agents.

- [Airbyte Agents](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents.md): Airbyte Agents is a data and context layer for AI agents. It gives your agents real-time access to business data through open source, type-safe connectors, managed credentials, and low-latency search. Use it as a cloud platform or import connectors directly into your own agents.

### admin

Manage your Airbyte Agents account. This section covers billing, including plans, payments, usage monitoring, invoices, and subscription changes. If your network restricts inbound traffic, see IP allow list.

- [Account and administration](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin.md): Manage your Airbyte Agents account. This section covers billing, including plans, payments, usage monitoring, invoices, and subscription changes. If your network restricts inbound traffic, see IP allow list.

#### billing

Airbyte Agents bills you based on a unit of measurement called agent operations (AOs). All plans come with a specific number of free AOs, and most plans allow you to exceed this limit for an additional cost. Your plan determines:

- [Billing and pricing](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin/billing.md): Airbyte Agents bills you based on a unit of measurement called agent operations (AOs). All plans come with a specific number of free AOs, and most plans allow you to exceed this limit for an additional cost. Your plan determines:

#### ip-allowlist

Airbyte Agents uses the Airbyte Cloud IP addresses, plus additional IP addresses for Agents-specific workloads. If your organization restricts inbound traffic by IP address, allow the following addresses in your firewall.

- [IP allow list for Agents](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin/ip-allowlist.md): Airbyte Agents uses the Airbyte Cloud IP addresses, plus additional IP addresses for Agents-specific workloads. If your organization restricts inbound traffic by IP address, allow the following addresses in your firewall.

#### profile

Your Profile page contains your personal account details, your organization's name, and the API credentials Airbyte Agents uses to authenticate programmatic access. Go to the Profile page to review these details or make changes.

- [Manage your user profile](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin/profile.md): Your Profile page contains your personal account details, your organization's name, and the API credentials Airbyte Agents uses to authenticate programmatic access. Go to the Profile page to review these details or make changes.

#### sessions

The Sessions page shows a read-only history of every agent interaction in your workspace, along with token usage and the connectors each interaction used. Use it to audit what your agents did, troubleshoot unexpected results, and understand what's driving your agent operations (AOs).

- [Review sessions](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin/sessions.md): The Sessions page shows a read-only history of every agent interaction in your workspace, along with token usage and the connectors each interaction used. Use it to audit what your agents did, troubleshoot unexpected results, and understand what's driving your agent operations (AOs).

#### tool-calls

Airbyte Agents logs every tool call your agents make. Review this log to understand what your agents are doing, troubleshoot failures, and investigate unexpected activity or cost spikes.

- [Review tool calls](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/admin/tool-calls.md): Airbyte Agents logs every tool call your agents make. Review this log to understand what your agents are doing, troubleshoot failures, and investigate unexpected activity or cost spikes.

### concepts

This section covers the building blocks of Airbyte Agents: the models, resources, and platform behaviors you work with across every interface.

- [Core concepts](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts.md): This section covers the building blocks of Airbyte Agents: the models, resources, and platform behaviors you work with across every interface.

#### agent-operations

An Agent Operation (AO) is the unit of work in Airbyte Agents. Every time an agent processes a prompt, reasons about data, or calls a tool through Airbyte's hosted platform, it consumes AOs. AOs measure the processing intensity of a task, not just the number of requests. Connector calls made locally through the open-source SDK do not consume AOs.

- [Agent operations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/agent-operations.md): An Agent Operation (AO) is the unit of work in Airbyte Agents. Every time an agent processes a prompt, reasons about data, or calls a tool through Airbyte's hosted platform, it consumes AOs. AOs measure the processing intensity of a task, not just the number of requests. Connector calls made locally through the open-source SDK do not consume AOs.

#### architecture

Airbyte Agents is a cloud platform that gives AI agents authenticated, structured access to third-party SaaS data. It stores credentials, manages token refresh, and exposes a uniform execution interface so agents can read, search, and write data across dozens of services.

- [System architecture](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/architecture.md): Airbyte Agents is a cloud platform that gives AI agents authenticated, structured access to third-party SaaS data. It stores credentials, manages token refresh, and exposes a uniform execution interface so agents can read, search, and write data across dozens of services.

##### connectors-and-credentials

A connector in Airbyte Agents is a stored credential and configuration for a third-party service. Connectors are what agents use to read, search, and write data in external systems. Each connector lives inside a workspace and is available to every interface that can access that workspace.

- [Connectors and credentials](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/architecture/connectors-and-credentials.md): A connector in Airbyte Agents is a stored credential and configuration for a third-party service. Connectors are what agents use to read, search, and write data in external systems. Each connector lives inside a workspace and is available to every interface that can access that workspace.

##### organizations

An organization is the top-level container in Airbyte Agents. It represents a single account, maps to one billing subscription, and owns every workspace, connector, and credential beneath it.

- [Organizations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/architecture/organizations.md): An organization is the top-level container in Airbyte Agents. It represents a single account, maps to one billing subscription, and owns every workspace, connector, and credential beneath it.

##### workspaces

A workspace is an isolation boundary within an organization. Each workspace holds its own set of connectors and credentials. A token scoped to one workspace cannot access connectors in another.

- [Workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/architecture/workspaces.md): A workspace is an isolation boundary within an organization. Each workspace holds its own set of connectors and credentials. A token scoped to one workspace cannot access connectors in another.

#### connect-ask-act

AI agents need real-time access to business data spread across dozens of systems, but building and maintaining those integrations is expensive and fragile. Airbyte Agents solves this with three layers: Connect your agents to any system, Ask questions across all your data in one searchable layer, and let agents Act on that data in real time.

- [Connect, Ask, Act](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/connect-ask-act.md): AI agents need real-time access to business data spread across dozens of systems, but building and maintaining those integrations is expensive and fragile. Airbyte Agents solves this with three layers: Connect your agents to any system, Ask questions across all your data in one searchable layer, and let agents Act on that data in real time.

#### context-store

The Context Store is a managed, searchable replica of select entities from all your connected data sources. Airbyte populates it from the connectors in your workspace and gives agents a fast, consistent way to search your business data without hitting the underlying APIs for every request.

- [Context Store](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/context-store.md): The Context Store is a managed, searchable replica of select entities from all your connected data sources. Airbyte populates it from the connectors in your workspace and gives agents a fast, consistent way to search your business data without hitting the underlying APIs for every request.

#### time-zones

Airbyte Agents handles dates and times the same way across every interface: display in your local time, and store and transport in UTC. This page explains how that works and what to expect in each interface.

- [Time zones](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/concepts/time-zones.md): Airbyte Agents handles dates and times the same way across every interface: display in your local time, and store and transport in UTC. This page explains how that works and what to expect in each interface.

### connectors

Airbyte's agent connectors equip AI agents to call third-party APIs through strongly typed, well-documented tools. All connectors ship inside the single airbyte-agent-sdk Python package and are ready to use in Airbyte Agents through any of the supported interfaces.

- [Agent connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/connectors.md): Airbyte's agent connectors equip AI agents to call third-party APIs through strongly typed, well-documented tools. All connectors ship inside the single airbyte-agent-sdk Python package and are ready to use in Airbyte Agents through any of the supported interfaces.

#### airtable

The Airtable agent connector is a Python package that equips AI agents to interact with Airtable through strongly typed, well-documented tools. It's ready to use directly in your Python app, in an agent framework, or exposed through an MCP.

- [Airtable](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/connectors/airtable.md): The Airtable agent connector is a Python package that equips AI agents to interact with Airtable through strongly typed, well-documented tools. It's ready to use directly in your Python app, in an agent framework, or exposed through an MCP.

### get-started

New to Airbyte Agents? Start here. Learn what the product is, choose the right interface for your use case, or jump straight into building. Sign up at app.airbyte.ai.

- [Get started](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started.md): New to Airbyte Agents? Start here. Learn what the product is, choose the right interface for your use case, or jump straight into building. Sign up at app.airbyte.ai.

#### choose-how-to-use

Airbyte Agents offers several interfaces. They all share the same platform, the same connectors, and the same Context Store, so you can start with one and add others as your needs grow.

- [Choose how to use Airbyte Agents](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/choose-how-to-use.md): Airbyte Agents offers several interfaces. They all share the same platform, the same connectors, and the same Context Store, so you can start with one and add others as your needs grow.

#### developer-quickstart

This section is for developers who want to build agents that use Airbyte connectors. Pick a path based on how you prefer to work.

- [Developer quickstart](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart.md): This section is for developers who want to build agents that use Airbyte connectors. Pick a path based on how you prefer to work.

##### skills

Skills are self-contained packages of context and instructions you give to an AI agent so it can generate working code against Airbyte. A skill teaches the agent the architecture, endpoints, authentication flow, and code patterns it needs to integrate Airbyte agent connectors into whatever it's building for you.

- [Skills](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/skills.md): Skills are self-contained packages of context and instructions you give to an AI agent so it can generate working code against Airbyte. A skill teaches the agent the architecture, endpoints, authentication flow, and code patterns it needs to integrate Airbyte agent connectors into whatever it's building for you.
- [Claude Code](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/skills/claude-code.md): Claude Code is the coding agent from Anthropic that runs in your terminal and integrates with editors like VS Code and Cursor. The airbyte-agent-sdk repository publishes a set of Claude skills that teach Claude Code how to build agents on top of the Airbyte typed Python SDK. Once you install the skills, Claude Code reads them on demand whenever you ask it to work with Airbyte connectors.
- [Codex](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/skills/codex.md): Codex is the coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally in your terminal and loads skills from ~/.codex/skills/. The airbyte-agent-sdk repository publishes a set of Codex skills that teach Codex how to build agents on top of the Airbyte typed Python SDK. Once you install the skills, Codex reads them on demand whenever you ask it to work with Airbyte connectors.
- [Lovable](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/skills/lovable.md): Lovable is an AI app builder that generates full-stack React and Supabase applications from natural-language prompts. Lovable doesn't expose a dedicated "skills" surface, but you can give it the same context two different ways: paste the skill directly into the prompt you use to build the app, or add it to Project/Workspace Knowledge.

##### tutorial-fastmcp

In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, build a FastMCP server that exposes one of Airbyte's agent connectors as an MCP tool, and use it to query GitHub data from any MCP-compatible agent. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

- [FastMCP quickstart](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/tutorial-fastmcp.md): In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, build a FastMCP server that exposes one of Airbyte's agent connectors as an MCP tool, and use it to query GitHub data from any MCP-compatible agent. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

##### tutorial-langchain

In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, add a LangChain agent, equip it with one of Airbyte's agent connectors, and use natural language to explore your data. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

- [LangChain quickstart](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/tutorial-langchain.md): In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, add a LangChain agent, equip it with one of Airbyte's agent connectors, and use natural language to explore your data. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, add a Pydantic AI agent, equip it with one of Airbyte's agent connectors, and use natural language to explore your data. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

- [Pydantic AI quickstart](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/developer-quickstart/tutorial-pydantic.md): In this tutorial, you'll create a new Python project with uv, add a Pydantic AI agent, equip it with one of Airbyte's agent connectors, and use natural language to explore your data. This tutorial uses GitHub, but if you don't have a GitHub account you can swap in any other agent connector and perform different operations.

#### what-is-airbyte-agents

Airbyte Agents gives AI agents reliable, real-time access to your business data. It connects agents to the tools your organization runs on, unifies that data into one searchable layer, and lets agents read, search, and write across every connected system.

- [What is Airbyte Agents?](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/get-started/what-is-airbyte-agents.md): Airbyte Agents gives AI agents reliable, real-time access to your business data. It connects agents to the tools your organization runs on, unifies that data into one searchable layer, and lets agents read, search, and write across every connected system.

### interfaces

Airbyte Agents supports several interfaces for working with your data and your agents. Choose the interface that best fits how you want to build and run agents.

- [Interfaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces.md): Airbyte Agents supports several interfaces for working with your data and your agents. Choose the interface that best fits how you want to build and run agents.

#### api

The Agent API lets you manage connectors, credentials, and data operations programmatically over HTTP. Use it to integrate Airbyte Agents into any language or framework, or to build custom backend services that interact with third-party data sources.

- [API](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/api.md): The Agent API lets you manage connectors, credentials, and data operations programmatically over HTTP. Use it to integrate Airbyte Agents into any language or framework, or to build custom backend services that interact with third-party data sources.

##### add-connector

A connector in Airbyte Agents is a stored set of credentials for a third-party service plus everything needed to execute operations against it. You create a connector once, then reuse the returned connector ID on every subsequent call.

- [Add a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/api/add-connector.md): A connector in Airbyte Agents is a stored set of credentials for a third-party service plus everything needed to execute operations against it. You create a connector once, then reuse the returned connector ID on every subsequent call.

##### authentication

You authenticate with the Agent API using your Airbyte Agents client credentials. Airbyte stores the credentials for each connector securely and mints short-lived tokens for your backend to call.

- [Authenticate](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/api/authentication.md): You authenticate with the Agent API using your Airbyte Agents client credentials. Airbyte stores the credentials for each connector securely and mints short-lived tokens for your backend to call.

##### execute

You can execute operations directly through the Agent API. This approach is useful when you're not using Python, when building custom integrations, or when you need to execute operations from a backend service.

- [Execute operations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/api/execute.md): You can execute operations directly through the Agent API. This approach is useful when you're not using Python, when building custom integrations, or when you need to execute operations from a backend service.

##### workspaces

Listing every workspace, updating a workspace's status, deleting a workspace, and reading workspace metadata are exposed through the API only. The SDK's workspace class covers what most apps need day-to-day; come here for the administrative operations on top.

- [Manage workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/api/workspaces.md): Listing every workspace, updating a workspace's status, deleting a workspace, and reading workspace metadata are exposed through the API only. The SDK's workspace class covers what most apps need day-to-day; come here for the administrative operations on top.

#### cli

The Airbyte Agent CLI (airbyte-agent) is a Go command-line interface for Airbyte Agents. Use it from a terminal, script, CI job, or agent harness to list workspaces, add connectors, inspect connector schemas, and execute connector actions.

- [CLI](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli.md): The Airbyte Agent CLI (airbyte-agent) is a Go command-line interface for Airbyte Agents. Use it from a terminal, script, CI job, or agent harness to list workspaces, add connectors, inspect connector schemas, and execute connector actions.

##### add-connector

A connector stores credentials and configuration for a third-party service in an Airbyte Agents workspace. Create a connector once, then reference it by id when you describe it or execute actions.

- [Add a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/add-connector.md): A connector stores credentials and configuration for a third-party service in an Airbyte Agents workspace. Create a connector once, then reference it by id when you describe it or execute actions.

##### authenticate

The CLI needs three values to call the Airbyte Agent API:

- [Authenticate](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/authenticate.md): The CLI needs three values to call the Airbyte Agent API:

##### command-reference

Run airbyte-agent --help to list top-level commands, airbyte-agent  --help to list operations, and airbyte-agent   --help for operation flags.

- [Command reference](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/command-reference.md): Run airbyte-agent --help to list top-level commands, airbyte-agent  --help to list operations, and airbyte-agent   --help for operation flags.

##### describe-connector

Use connectors describe to inspect a configured connector before executing actions against it. The response includes the connector details plus a schema object returned by the connector's describe action.

- [Describe a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/describe-connector.md): Use connectors describe to inspect a configured connector before executing actions against it. The response includes the connector details plus a schema object returned by the connector's describe action.

##### execute

connectors execute runs an action against an entity on a configured connector. Use it for reads, searches, creates, and updates.

- [Execute operations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/execute.md): connectors execute runs an action against an entity on a configured connector. Use it for reads, searches, creates, and updates.

##### troubleshooting

Use the JSON error on stderr as the primary signal. Exit codes are useful, but the type, message, and hint fields usually tell you what to fix.

- [Troubleshoot the CLI](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/troubleshooting.md): Use the JSON error on stderr as the primary signal. Exit codes are useful, but the type, message, and hint fields usually tell you what to fix.

##### using-with-ai-agents

AI agents can call airbyte-agent as a shell tool. The CLI gives agents a consistent command model, JSON input and output, and runtime schema discovery.

- [Use the CLI with AI agents](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/using-with-ai-agents.md): AI agents can call airbyte-agent as a shell tool. The CLI gives agents a consistent command model, JSON input and output, and runtime schema discovery.

##### workspaces

Use workspaces commands to list workspaces and save a default workspace. Use organizations commands to list organizations and save a default organization.

- [Manage workspaces and organizations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/cli/workspaces.md): Use workspaces commands to list workspaces and save a default workspace. Use organizations commands to list organizations and save a default organization.

#### mcp

The Agent MCP connects your AI agent to your data through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It gives your agent authenticated access to the platforms you use every day, like your CRM, support desk, analytics tools, and more, so your agent can read and write data on your behalf. See Connectors for a list of available connectors.

- [Agent MCP](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/mcp.md): The Agent MCP connects your AI agent to your data through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It gives your agent authenticated access to the platforms you use every day, like your CRM, support desk, analytics tools, and more, so your agent can read and write data on your behalf. See Connectors for a list of available connectors.

#### sdk

The Agent SDK (airbyteagentsdk) is the Python interface for Airbyte Agents. With one install you get typed connectors, automatic credential handling, direct execution, and patterns for exposing connectors as tools to AI agent frameworks.

- [SDK](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/sdk.md): The Agent SDK (airbyteagentsdk) is the Python interface for Airbyte Agents. With one install you get typed connectors, automatic credential handling, direct execution, and patterns for exposing connectors as tools to AI agent frameworks.

##### add-connector

List, get, and delete connectors for third-party services.

- [Add a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/sdk/add-connector.md): List, get, and delete connectors for third-party services.

##### authenticate

The SDK authenticates with Airbyte Agents using an Airbyte clientid and clientsecret. Once the SDK has these, it handles the rest: fetching tokens, refreshing them before they expire, and attaching them to every request. You never manage tokens yourself.

- [Authenticate](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/sdk/authenticate.md): The SDK authenticates with Airbyte Agents using an Airbyte clientid and clientsecret. Once the SDK has these, it handles the rest: fetching tokens, refreshing them before they expire, and attaching them to every request. You never manage tokens yourself.

##### execute

Once you've added a connector to your workspace, you can run operations against it from Python. The SDK offers direct execution and patterns for exposing a connector as a tool to an AI agent framework.

- [Execute operations](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/sdk/execute.md): Once you've added a connector to your workspace, you can run operations against it from Python. The SDK offers direct execution and patterns for exposing a connector as a tool to an AI agent framework.

##### workspaces

A workspace is a container inside your Airbyte Agents organization that holds a set of connectors and credentials. A token scoped to one workspace can't reach another.

- [Manage workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/sdk/workspaces.md): A workspace is a container inside your Airbyte Agents organization that holds a set of connectors and credentials. A token scoped to one workspace can't reach another.

#### ui

The Airbyte Agents web app at app.airbyte.ai is the fastest way to use Airbyte Agents without writing code. Describe what you want in natural language, and Airbyte picks the right connectors, makes the necessary tool calls, and replies with an answer grounded in your data.

- [Web app](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/ui.md): The Airbyte Agents web app at app.airbyte.ai is the fastest way to use Airbyte Agents without writing code. Describe what you want in natural language, and Airbyte picks the right connectors, makes the necessary tool calls, and replies with an answer grounded in your data.

##### add-connector

Before an Airbyte agent can read from or write to a data source, someone has to authenticate that source for the workspace. In the web app, that happens on the Connectors page. Adding a connector means picking a workspace, picking a data source, and completing an authentication flow once; after that, every interface you use (Chats, the SDK, the API, and the MCP server) can use the resulting connector.

- [Add a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/ui/add-connector.md): Before an Airbyte agent can read from or write to a data source, someone has to authenticate that source for the workspace. In the web app, that happens on the Connectors page. Adding a connector means picking a workspace, picking a data source, and completing an authentication flow once; after that, every interface you use (Chats, the SDK, the API, and the MCP server) can use the resulting connector.

##### chats

A Chat is a conversation between you and an Airbyte agent in the web app. You send a prompt, the agent decides which connectors to use and which tool calls to make, and it replies with an answer grounded in your data. Chats are the fastest way to explore data, get a one-off answer, or prototype an idea.

- [Chats](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/interfaces/ui/chats.md): A Chat is a conversation between you and an Airbyte agent in the web app. You send a prompt, the agent decides which connectors to use and which tool calls to make, and it replies with an answer grounded in your data. Chats are the fastest way to explore data, get a one-off answer, or prototype an idea.

##### api-reference

- [Airbyte Agent API](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/airbyte-agent-api.md): This is the public API documentation for Airbyte's Agent API. Use the API to manage authentication, connectors, and workspaces, and power their agentic workflows.
- [Authentication](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/authentication.md): Authentication
- [Authentication (Advanced)](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/authentication-advanced.md): Authentication (Advanced)
- [Connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/connectors.md): Connectors
- [Connectors (Advanced)](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/connectors-advanced.md): Connectors (Advanced)
- [Create Scoped Token](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-account-applications-scoped-token.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Generate Application Token](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-account-applications-token.md): Generate an application access token using client credentials. This endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated - authentication is performed via client_id and client_secret in the request body. Returns a self-signed JWT token that can be used for all API calls.
- [Create Widget Token](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-account-applications-widget-token.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Create a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-connectors.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Check config when creating a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-connectors-check.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Check config when updating a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-connectors-id-check.md): Check source configuration before updating an existing source.
- [Execute actions](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-connectors-id-execute.md): Execute a connector operation using an Airbyte Platform connector ID.
- [Create Connection Template](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-templates-connections.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Describe Cron Expression](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-templates-connections-cron-describe.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Enable a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/create-integrations-templates-sources.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Data replication](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/data-replication.md): Data replication
- [Delete a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/delete-integrations-connectors-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Delete Connection Template](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/delete-integrations-templates-connections-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Disable a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/delete-integrations-templates-sources-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Delete connector OAuth](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/delete-oauth-credentials-connector-type-connector-type.md): Delete OAuth credentials for the user's organization.
- [Delete Workspace](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/delete-workspaces-workspace-id.md): Delete a workspace. Removes the workspace from the Data Replication Platform and soft-deletes locally.
- [Get Scoped Token Info](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-account-applications-scoped-token-info.md): **Requires a Scoped Token as the bearer token.**
- [Get a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-connectors-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Inspect connector metadata and readiness](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-connectors-id-inspect.md): Return metadata, context-store readiness, and available skills for a configured connector.
- [Get Destination Definition](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-definitions-destinations-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Get a connector definition](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-definitions-sources-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Get Connection Template](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-templates-connections-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Get an enabled connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-integrations-templates-sources-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Read skill docs](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-skills-docs.md): Retrieve documentation for a skill, optionally scoped to a specific section.
- [Get Workspace Stats](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-workspaces-stats.md): Get workspace statistics for the authenticated organization.
- [Get Workspace](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/get-workspaces-workspace-id.md): Get a single workspace by ID.
- [List connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-integrations-connectors.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [List Destination Definitions](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-integrations-definitions-destinations.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [List connector definitions](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-integrations-definitions-sources.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [List Connection Templates](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-integrations-templates-connections.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [List enabled connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-integrations-templates-sources.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [List skills](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-skills.md): Return a paginated list of skills available to the caller's organization and workspace.
- [Search skills](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-skills-search.md): Search skills by keyword query, returning a paginated list of matching results.
- [List Workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/list-workspaces.md): List workspaces for the authenticated organization with cursor-based pagination.
- [Skills](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/skills.md): Skills
- [Update a connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/update-integrations-connectors-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Patch Connection Template](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/update-integrations-templates-connections-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Update an enabled connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/update-integrations-templates-sources-id.md): **Requires an Access Token as the bearer token.**
- [Configure connector OAuth](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/update-oauth-credentials.md): Create or update OAuth credentials for the user's organization.
- [Update Workspace](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/update-workspaces-workspace-id.md): Update a workspace's name, status, color, and/or cache setting.
- [Workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/api/api-reference/workspaces.md): Workspaces

#### sdk

Complete reference for the Agent SDK (airbyteagentsdk). For a guided introduction, authentication, and example code, see the SDK interface documentation.

- [SDK reference](https://docs.airbyte.io/ai-agents/reference/sdk.md): Complete reference for the Agent SDK (airbyteagentsdk). For a guided introduction, authentication, and example code, see the SDK interface documentation.

### licenses

Airbyte Connectors and everything in our public repos excluding the airbytehq/airbyte-protocol are open sourced and available under the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2) License. Each connector's metadata.yaml file contains more information.

- [Licenses](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/licenses.md): Airbyte Connectors and everything in our public repos excluding the airbytehq/airbyte-protocol are open sourced and available under the Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2) License. Each connector's metadata.yaml file contains more information.

#### elv2-license

Elastic License 2.0 \(ELv2\)

- [ELv2](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/licenses/elv2-license.md): Elastic License 2.0 \(ELv2\)

#### examples

We chose ELv2 because it's permissive with what you can do with the software. To be as explicit as possible, here are examples of projects you can and can't do.

- [Examples](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/licenses/examples.md): We chose ELv2 because it's permissive with what you can do with the software. To be as explicit as possible, here are examples of projects you can and can't do.

### mcp-servers

Airbyte provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for connecting AI assistants to Airbyte and Airbyte-related context.

- [MCP servers](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/mcp-servers.md): Airbyte provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for connecting AI assistants to Airbyte and Airbyte-related context.

#### airbyte-knowledge-mcp

The Airbyte knowledge MCP server connects AI agents to comprehensive sources of information about Airbyte. It provides semantic search over Airbyte's documentation, website, OpenAPI specs, YouTube content, and GitHub issues, discussions, and pull requests.

- [Airbyte knowledge MCP server](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/mcp-servers/airbyte-knowledge-mcp.md): The Airbyte knowledge MCP server connects AI agents to comprehensive sources of information about Airbyte. It provides semantic search over Airbyte's documentation, website, OpenAPI specs, YouTube content, and GitHub issues, discussions, and pull requests.

#### replication-mcp

This MCP server implementation is experimental and may change without notice between minor versions of PyAirbyte. The API may be modified or entirely refactored in future versions.

- [Airbyte Replication MCP Server](https://docs.airbyte.io/community/mcp-servers/replication-mcp.md): This MCP server implementation is experimental and may change without notice between minor versions of PyAirbyte. The API may be modified or entirely refactored in future versions.

### pyairbyte

#### reference

This section contains the auto-generated API reference documentation for PyAirbyte.

- [PyAirbyte API Reference](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference.md): This section contains the auto-generated API reference documentation for PyAirbyte.

##### airbyte

PyAirbyte brings the power of Airbyte to every Python developer.

- [Module airbyte](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte.md): PyAirbyte brings the power of Airbyte to every Python developer.
- [Module airbyte.callbacks](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-callbacks.md): Callbacks for working with PyAirbyte.
- [Module airbyte.cli](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-cli.md): CLI for PyAirbyte.
- [Module airbyte.constants](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-constants.md): Constants shared across the PyAirbyte codebase.
- [Module airbyte.documents](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-documents.md): This module contains the Documents class for converting Airbyte records into documents.
- [Module airbyte.exceptions](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-exceptions.md): All exceptions used in the PyAirbyte.
- [Module airbyte.logs](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-logs.md): PyAirbyte Logging features and related configuration.
- [Module airbyte.progress](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-progress.md): A simple progress bar for the command line and IPython notebooks.
- [Module airbyte.records](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-records.md): PyAirbyte Records module.
- [Module airbyte.registry](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-registry.md): Connectivity to the connector catalog registry.
- [Module airbyte.results](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-results.md): Module which defines the ReadResult and WriteResult classes.
- [Module airbyte.strategies](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-strategies.md): Read and write strategies for PyAirbyte.
- [Module airbyte.types](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-types.md): Type conversion methods for SQL Caches.
- [Module airbyte.validate](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-validate.md): Defines the airbyte-lib-validate-source CLI.
- [Module airbyte.version](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/airbyte-version.md): Support for PyAirbyte version checks.
- [Module airbyte.caches](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches.md): Base module for all caches.
- [Module airbyte.caches.base](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-base.md): SQL Cache implementation.
- [Module airbyte.caches.bigquery](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-bigquery.md): A BigQuery implementation of the cache.
- [Module airbyte.caches.duckdb](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-duckdb.md): A DuckDB implementation of the PyAirbyte cache.
- [Module airbyte.caches.generic](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-generic.md): A Generic SQL Cache implementation.
- [Module airbyte.caches.motherduck](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-motherduck.md): A MotherDuck implementation of the PyAirbyte cache, built on DuckDB.
- [Module airbyte.caches.postgres](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-postgres.md): A Postgres implementation of the PyAirbyte cache.
- [Module airbyte.caches.snowflake](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-snowflake.md): A Snowflake implementation of the PyAirbyte cache.
- [Module airbyte.caches.util](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/caches/airbyte-caches-util.md): Utility functions for working with caches.
- [Module airbyte.cloud](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud.md): PyAirbyte classes and methods for interacting with the Airbyte Cloud API.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.auth](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-auth.md): Authentication-related constants and utilities for the Airbyte Cloud.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.client_config](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-client_config.md): Cloud client configuration for Airbyte Cloud API authentication.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.connections](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-connections.md): Cloud Connections.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-connectors.md): Cloud connectors module for working with Cloud sources and destinations.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.constants](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-constants.md): Useful constants for working with Airbyte Cloud features in PyAirbyte.
- [Module airbyte.cloud.sync_results](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/cloud/airbyte-cloud-sync_results.md): Sync results for Airbyte Cloud workspaces.

- [Module airbyte.mcp.cloud](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/pyairbyte/reference/airbyte/mcp/airbyte-mcp-cloud.md): Airbyte Cloud MCP operations.

### terraform-documentation

Terraform, developed by HashiCorp, is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool that empowers you to define and provision infrastructure using a declarative configuration language. If you use Terraform to manage your infrastructure, you can use Airbyte's Terraform provider to automate and version control your Airbyte configuration as code. Airbyte's Terraform provider is built off Airbyte's API.

- [Terraform provider](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/terraform-documentation.md): Terraform, developed by HashiCorp, is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool that empowers you to define and provision infrastructure using a declarative configuration language. If you use Terraform to manage your infrastructure, you can use Airbyte's Terraform provider to automate and version control your Airbyte configuration as code. Airbyte's Terraform provider is built off Airbyte's API.

### terraform-provider-pre-1.0

This tutorial covers the pre-1.0 Terraform provider, which used typed connector-specific resources (e.g., airbytesourcestripe) and weakly typed JSON resources (e.g., airbytesourcecustom). These resource types are deprecated in provider 1.0+.

- [Terraform provider — Pre-1.0 getting started](https://docs.airbyte.io/developers/terraform-provider-pre-1.0.md): This tutorial covers the pre-1.0 Terraform provider, which used typed connector-specific resources (e.g., airbytesourcestripe) and weakly typed JSON resources (e.g., airbytesourcecustom). These resource types are deprecated in provider 1.0+.

## integrations

Airbyte's library of connectors is used by the data replication platform. A connector is a tool to pull data from a source or push data to a destination. To learn more about connectors, see Sources, destinations, and connectors. To learn how to use a specific connector, find the documentation for the connector you want to use, below.

- [Data replication connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations.md): Airbyte's library of connectors is used by the data replication platform. A connector is a tool to pull data from a source or push data to a destination. To learn more about connectors, see Sources, destinations, and connectors. To learn how to use a specific connector, find the documentation for the connector you want to use, below.

### connector-support-levels

The following table describes the support levels of Airbyte connectors.

- [Connector support levels](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations/connector-support-levels.md): The following table describes the support levels of Airbyte connectors.

### custom-connectors

Missing a connector?

- [Custom or New Connector](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations/custom-connectors.md): Missing a connector?

### destinations

Destination connectors are the data warehouses, data lakes, databases, or analytics tools to which you want to push data. Each connector has one of three support levels. Review Connector support levels for details on each tier.

- [Destinations](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations/destinations.md): Destination connectors are the data warehouses, data lakes, databases, or analytics tools to which you want to push data. Each connector has one of three support levels. Review Connector support levels for details on each tier.

### enterprise-connectors


#### destination-salesforce

The Salesforce destination connector enables data activation by syncing data from your data warehouse to Salesforce objects. This connector is designed for operational workflows where you need to deliver modeled data directly to your CRM for sales, marketing, and customer success teams.

- [Salesforce destination](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations/enterprise-connectors/destination-salesforce.md): The Salesforce destination connector enables data activation by syncing data from your data warehouse to Salesforce objects. This connector is designed for operational workflows where you need to deliver modeled data directly to your CRM for sales, marketing, and customer success teams.

### sources

Source connectors connect to the APIs, file, databases, or data warehouses from which you want to pull data. Each connector has one of three support levels. Review Connector support levels for details on each tier.

- [Sources](https://docs.airbyte.io/integrations/sources.md): Source connectors connect to the APIs, file, databases, or data warehouses from which you want to pull data. Each connector has one of three support levels. Review Connector support levels for details on each tier.

### speed-improvements

Airbyte has made major investments into the platform's sync speed. This page explains what you need to know about these speed improvements and how you can take advantage of them.

## platform

Use Airbyte's data replication platform to consolidate data from hundreds of sources into your data warehouses, data lakes, and databases. Then, move data into the operational tools where work happens, like CRMs, marketing platforms, and support systems.

- [Data replication platform](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform.md): Use Airbyte's data replication platform to consolidate data from hundreds of sources into your data warehouses, data lakes, and databases. Then, move data into the operational tools where work happens, like CRMs, marketing platforms, and support systems.

### access-management


#### rbac

Role Based Access Control allows a user with Administrative access to apply roles to users, granting different levels of permission within an organization or workspace.

- [Role-based access control (RBAC)](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/access-management/rbac.md): Role Based Access Control allows a user with Administrative access to apply roles to users, granting different levels of permission within an organization or workspace.

#### role-mapping

Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) role mapping allows automatic assignment of specific permissions to Airbyte users based on existing roles in your organization. It ensures users have appropriate Airbyte access without manual oversight.

- [RBAC Role Mapping](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/access-management/role-mapping.md): Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) role mapping allows automatic assignment of specific permissions to Airbyte users based on existing roles in your organization. It ensures users have appropriate Airbyte access without manual oversight.

#### sso

Use Open ID Connect (OIDC) to log into Airbyte using an Identity Provider (IdP) like Okta or Entra ID/Active Directory.

- [Single sign on (SSO)](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/access-management/sso.md): Use Open ID Connect (OIDC) to log into Airbyte using an Identity Provider (IdP) like Okta or Entra ID/Active Directory.

#### sso-providers


##### azure-entra-id

This guide shows you how to set up Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure ActiveDirectory) and Airbyte so your users can log into Airbyte using your organization's identity provider (IdP) and OpenID Connect (OIDC).

- [Set up single sign on using Entra ID](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/access-management/sso-providers/azure-entra-id.md): This guide shows you how to set up Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure ActiveDirectory) and Airbyte so your users can log into Airbyte using your organization's identity provider (IdP) and OpenID Connect (OIDC).

##### okta

This guide shows you how to set up Okta and Airbyte so your users can log into Airbyte using your organization's identity provider (IdP).

- [Set up single sign on using Okta](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/access-management/sso-providers/okta.md): This guide shows you how to set up Okta and Airbyte so your users can log into Airbyte using your organization's identity provider (IdP).

### cloud


#### managing-airbyte-cloud


##### configuring-connections

After you set up a connection, you may need to monitor, update, or repair it. You can do this from any connections' page. Airbyte also takes you to this page after you finish configuring a connection.

- [Manage existing connections](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/configuring-connections.md): After you set up a connection, you may need to monitor, update, or repair it. You can do this from any connections' page. Airbyte also takes you to this page after you finish configuring a connection.

##### dbt-cloud-integration

By using the dbt Cloud integration, you can create and run dbt transformations immediately following syncs in Airbyte Cloud. This allows you to transform raw data into a format that is suitable for analysis and reporting, including cleaning and enriching the data.

- [dbt Cloud integration](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/dbt-cloud-integration.md): By using the dbt Cloud integration, you can create and run dbt transformations immediately following syncs in Airbyte Cloud. This allows you to transform raw data into a format that is suitable for analysis and reporting, including cleaning and enriching the data.

##### manage-airbyte-cloud-notifications

If you want Airbyte to notify you about important events, use its built-in notification system.

- [Manage notifications](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/manage-airbyte-cloud-notifications.md): If you want Airbyte to notify you about important events, use its built-in notification system.

##### manage-connection-state

The connection state provides additional information about incremental syncs. It includes the most recent values for the global or stream-level cursors, which can aid in debugging or determining which data will be included in the next sync.

- [Modifying connection state](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/manage-connection-state.md): The connection state provides additional information about incremental syncs. It includes the most recent values for the global or stream-level cursors, which can aid in debugging or determining which data will be included in the next sync.

##### manage-credits

In order to manage your payment and billing information, you need the Organization Admin role.

- [Manage billing and credits](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/manage-credits.md): In order to manage your payment and billing information, you need the Organization Admin role.

##### manage-data-residency

Your connections can run in the managed or self-managed region of your choice.

- [Set data residency](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/manage-data-residency.md): Your connections can run in the managed or self-managed region of your choice.

##### manage-data-workers

If you are on a capacity-based plan, you can monitor your data worker usage across your organization and understand how capacity enforcement affects your syncs. When all committed data workers are in use, newly triggered sync jobs are queued until capacity becomes available. To view data worker usage, you need the organization admin role.

- [Monitor data worker usage](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/manage-data-workers.md): If you are on a capacity-based plan, you can monitor your data worker usage across your organization and understand how capacity enforcement affects your syncs. When all committed data workers are in use, newly triggered sync jobs are queued until capacity becomes available. To view data worker usage, you need the organization admin role.

##### review-connection-status

The Connections page, and each connection within, give you tools to monitor the health of your connections. If something goes wrong, you can investigate further and find the root of the problem.

- [Connection status](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/review-connection-status.md): The Connections page, and each connection within, give you tools to monitor the health of your connections. If something goes wrong, you can investigate further and find the root of the problem.

##### review-connection-timeline

The Connection Timeline displays historical information about relevant connection events. You can also view and download logs, find any relevant errors, and find a link to a job to share with Support.

- [Connection timeline](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/review-connection-timeline.md): The Connection Timeline displays historical information about relevant connection events. You can also view and download logs, find any relevant errors, and find a link to a job to share with Support.

Understanding the following limitations will help you more effectively manage Airbyte Cloud.

- [Airbyte Cloud limits](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/cloud/managing-airbyte-cloud/understand-airbyte-cloud-limits.md): Understanding the following limitations will help you more effectively manage Airbyte Cloud.

### connector-development

If you'd like to build a connector that doesn't yet exist in Airbyte's catalog, in most cases you should use Connector Builder!

- [Connector Development](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development.md): If you'd like to build a connector that doesn't yet exist in Airbyte's catalog, in most cases you should use Connector Builder!

#### best-practices

In order to guarantee the highest quality for connectors, we've compiled the following best practices for connector development. Connectors which follow these best practices will be labelled as "Airbyte Certified" to indicate they've passed a high quality bar and will perform reliably in all production use cases. Following these guidelines is not required for your contribution to Airbyte to be accepted, as they add a barrier to entry for contribution \(though adopting them certainly doesn't hurt!\).

- [Best Practices](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/best-practices.md): In order to guarantee the highest quality for connectors, we've compiled the following best practices for connector development. Connectors which follow these best practices will be labelled as "Airbyte Certified" to indicate they've passed a high quality bar and will perform reliably in all production use cases. Following these guidelines is not required for your contribution to Airbyte to be accepted, as they add a barrier to entry for contribution \(though adopting them certainly doesn't hurt!\).

#### cdk-python

##### basic-concepts

The Airbyte Specification

- [Basic Concepts](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/basic-concepts.md): The Airbyte Specification

##### full-refresh-stream

As mentioned in the Basic Concepts Overview, a Stream is the atomic unit for reading data from a Source. A stream can read data from anywhere: a relational database, an API, or even scrape a web page! \(although that might be stretching the limits of what a connector should do\).

- [Full Refresh Streams](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/full-refresh-stream.md): As mentioned in the Basic Concepts Overview, a Stream is the atomic unit for reading data from a Source. A stream can read data from anywhere: a relational database, an API, or even scrape a web page! \(although that might be stretching the limits of what a connector should do\).

##### http-streams

The CDK offers base classes that greatly simplify writing HTTP API-based connectors. Some of the most useful features include helper functionality for:

- [HTTP-API-based Connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/http-streams.md): The CDK offers base classes that greatly simplify writing HTTP API-based connectors. Some of the most useful features include helper functionality for:

##### incremental-stream

An incremental Stream is a stream which reads data incrementally. That is, it only reads data that was generated or updated since the last time it ran, and is thus far more efficient than a stream which reads all the source data every time it runs. If possible, developers are encouraged to implement incremental streams to reduce sync times and resource usage.

- [Incremental Streams](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/incremental-stream.md): An incremental Stream is a stream which reads data incrementally. That is, it only reads data that was generated or updated since the last time it ran, and is thus far more efficient than a stream which reads all the source data every time it runs. If possible, developers are encouraged to implement incremental streams to reduce sync times and resource usage.

##### migration-to-base-image

We currently enforce our certified python connectors to use our base image.

- [Migration Guide: How to make a python connector use our base image](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/migration-to-base-image.md): We currently enforce our certified python connectors to use our base image.

##### resumable-full-refresh-stream

This feature is currently in-development. CDK interfaces and classes relating to this feature may change without notice.

- [Resumable Full Refresh Streams](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/resumable-full-refresh-stream.md): This feature is currently in-development. CDK interfaces and classes relating to this feature may change without notice.

##### schemas

Your connector must describe the schema of each stream it can output using JSONSchema.

- [Defining Stream Schemas](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/cdk-python/schemas.md): Your connector must describe the schema of each stream it can output using JSONSchema.

- [How the Framework Works](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/advanced-topics/how-framework-works.md): 1. Given the connection config and an optional stream state, the PartitionRouter computes the partitions that should be routed to read data.

- [Object Instantiation](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/advanced-topics/object-instantiation.md): If the component is a literal, then it is returned as is:
- [Parameters](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/advanced-topics/parameters.md): Parameters can be passed down from a parent component to its subcomponents using the $parameters key.
- [References](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/advanced-topics/references.md): Strings can contain references to previously defined values.
- [String Interpolation](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/advanced-topics/string-interpolation.md): String values can be evaluated as Jinja2 templates.

##### low-code-cdk-overview

Airbyte's low-code framework enables you to build source connectors for REST APIs via a connector builder UI or by modifying boilerplate YAML files via terminal or text editor. The low-code CDK is a part of the Python CDK that provides a mapping from connector manifest YAML files to actual behavior implementations.

- [Low-code connector development](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/low-code-cdk-overview.md): Airbyte's low-code framework enables you to build source connectors for REST APIs via a connector builder UI or by modifying boilerplate YAML files via terminal or text editor. The low-code CDK is a part of the Python CDK that provides a mapping from connector manifest YAML files to actual behavior implementations.

##### understanding-the-yaml-file

- [Authentication](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/authentication.md): The Authenticator defines how to configure outgoing HTTP requests to authenticate on the API source.
- [Error Handling](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/error-handling.md): By default, only server errors (HTTP 5XX) and too many requests (HTTP 429) will be retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff.
- [File Syncing](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/file-syncing.md): File syncing enables connectors to download and transfer files from API sources when an API endpoint returns a file. This capability supports all common file formats including documents, images, and structured data.
- [Incremental Sync](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/incremental-syncs.md): An incremental sync is a sync which pulls only the data that has changed since the previous sync (as opposed to all the data available in the data source).
- [Pagination](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/pagination.md): Given a page size and a pagination strategy, the DefaultPaginator will point to pages of results for as long as its strategy returns a nextpagetoken.
- [Partitions](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/partition-router.md): In some cases, the data you are replicating is spread across multiple partitions. You can specify a set of parameters to be iterated over and used while requesting all of your data. On each iteration, using the current element being iterated upon, the connector will perform a cycle of requesting data from your source.
- [Property Chunking](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/property-chunking.md): Property chunking enables connectors to handle APIs with limitations on the number of properties that you can fetch per request. This feature breaks down large property lists into smaller, manageable chunks and merges the results back into complete records. Some connectors require this capability to work with APIs that have property limits.
- [Rate Limiting (API Budget)](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/rate-limit-api-budget.md): In order to prevent sending too many requests to the API in a short period of time, you can configure an API Budget. This budget determines the maximum number of calls that can be made within a specified time interval (or intervals). This mechanism is particularly useful for respecting third-party API rate limits and avoiding potential throttling or denial of service.
- [Record Selector](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/record-selector.md): The record selector is responsible for translating an HTTP response into a list of Airbyte records by extracting records from the response and optionally filtering and shaping records based on a heuristic.
- [YAML Reference](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/reference.md): This page lists all components, interpolation variables and interpolation macros that can be used when defining a low code YAML file.
- [Request Options](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/request-options.md): The primary way to set request parameters and headers is to define them as key-value pairs using a RequestOptionsProvider.
- [Requester](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/requester.md): The Requester defines how to prepare HTTP requests to send to the source API.
- [YAML Components](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/config-based/understanding-the-yaml-file/yaml-overview.md): The low-code framework involves editing a boilerplate YAML file. This section deep dives into the components of the YAML file.

#### connector-breaking-changes

Whenever possible, changes to connectors should be implemented in a non-breaking way. This allows users to upgrade to the latest version of a connector without additional action required on their part. Assume that every breaking change creates friction for users and should be avoided except when absolutely necessary.

- [Managing Breaking Changes in Connectors](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/connector-breaking-changes.md): Whenever possible, changes to connectors should be implemented in a non-breaking way. This allows users to upgrade to the latest version of a connector without additional action required on their part. Assume that every breaking change creates friction for users and should be avoided except when absolutely necessary.

This is done to reduce the amount of waiting time in between test syncs.

##### global-configuration

Global Configuration settings in the Connector Builder UI allow you to define connector-wide behaviors that apply across all streams. These settings control how your connector validates connections, manages request concurrency, and handles API rate limiting.

- [Global Configuration](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/connector-builder-ui/global-configuration.md): Global Configuration settings in the Connector Builder UI allow you to define connector-wide behaviors that apply across all streams. These settings control how your connector validates connections, manages request concurrency, and handles API rate limiting.

##### overview

Connector Builder is a no-code tool that’s part of the Airbyte UI. It provides an intuitive user interface on top of the low-code YAML format, letting you develop a connector to use in data syncs without ever needing to leave your Airbyte workspace. You can seamlessly switch between the visual UI and direct YAML editing as needed. Connector Builder offers the most straightforward method for building, contributing to, and maintaining source connectors.

- [Connector Builder](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/connector-builder-ui/overview.md): Connector Builder is a no-code tool that’s part of the Airbyte UI. It provides an intuitive user interface on top of the low-code YAML format, letting you develop a connector to use in data syncs without ever needing to leave your Airbyte workspace. You can seamlessly switch between the visual UI and direct YAML editing as needed. Connector Builder offers the most straightforward method for building, contributing to, and maintaining source connectors.

##### pagination

Pagination is a mechanism used by APIs in which data is split up into "pages" when returning results, so that the entire response data doesn't need to be returned all at once.

- [Pagination](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/connector-builder-ui/pagination.md): Pagination is a mechanism used by APIs in which data is split up into "pages" when returning results, so that the entire response data doesn't need to be returned all at once.

##### partitioning

Partitioning is required when records of a stream are grouped into subsets that need to be queried separately to extract all records. This is common when APIs require specific parameters (like IDs or categories) to fetch different portions of the data.

- [Partitions](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/connector-development/connector-builder-ui/partitioning.md): Partitioning is required when records of a stream are grouped into subsets that need to be queried separately to extract all records. This is common when APIs require specific parameters (like IDs or categories) to fetch different portions of the data.

##### custom-image-registries

You can optionally configure Airbyte to pull Docker images from a custom image registry rather than Airbyte's public Docker repository. In this case, Airbyte pulls both platform images (e.g. server, workload-launcher, etc.) and connector images (e.g. Postgres Source, S3 Destination, etc.) from the configured registry.

- [Custom image registry](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/deploying-airbyte/integrations/custom-image-registries.md): You can optionally configure Airbyte to pull Docker images from a custom image registry rather than Airbyte's public Docker repository. In this case, Airbyte pulls both platform images (e.g. server, workload-launcher, etc.) and connector images (e.g. Postgres Source, S3 Destination, etc.) from the configured registry.

##### database

For production deployments, we recommend using a dedicated database instance for better reliability, and backups (such as AWS RDS or GCP Cloud SQL) instead of the default internal Postgres database (airbyte/db) that Airbyte spins up within the Kubernetes cluster.

- [External Database](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/deploying-airbyte/integrations/database.md): For production deployments, we recommend using a dedicated database instance for better reliability, and backups (such as AWS RDS or GCP Cloud SQL) instead of the default internal Postgres database (airbyte/db) that Airbyte spins up within the Kubernetes cluster.

### enterprise-flex

Airbyte Enterprise Flex is a hybrid solution that consists of a fully managed Cloud control plane that supports separate data planes that run in your own infrastructure. It's ideal for organizations with data sovereignty and compliance requirements who need to carefully manage data movement while also minimizing the time and effort needed to self-manage Airbyte.

- [Enterprise Flex](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/enterprise-flex.md): Airbyte Enterprise Flex is a hybrid solution that consists of a fully managed Cloud control plane that supports separate data planes that run in your own infrastructure. It's ideal for organizations with data sovereignty and compliance requirements who need to carefully manage data movement while also minimizing the time and effort needed to self-manage Airbyte.

#### data-plane

Airbyte Enterprise Flex customers can use Airbyte's public API to define regions and create independent data planes that operate in those regions. This ensures you're satisfying your data residency and governance requirements with a single Airbyte Cloud deployment, and it can help you reduce data egress costs with cloud providers.

- [Deploy a data plane with Helm in Enterprise Flex](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/enterprise-flex/data-plane.md): Airbyte Enterprise Flex customers can use Airbyte's public API to define regions and create independent data planes that operate in those regions. This ensures you're satisfying your data residency and governance requirements with a single Airbyte Cloud deployment, and it can help you reduce data egress costs with cloud providers.

#### data-plane-util

Airbox is Airbyte's command line tool for managing Airbyte data planes on Kubernetes. It's the ideal way to deploy and manage data planes for teams that have limited Kubernetes expertise or don't want to deploy with Helm.

- [Deploy a data plane with Airbox in Enterprise Flex](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/enterprise-flex/data-plane-util.md): Airbox is Airbyte's command line tool for managing Airbyte data planes on Kubernetes. It's the ideal way to deploy and manage data planes for teams that have limited Kubernetes expertise or don't want to deploy with Helm.

#### getting-started

Any Airbyte Cloud environment can upgrade to Enterprise Flex. To learn more about upgrading, talk to sales.

- [Get started with Enterprise Flex](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/enterprise-flex/getting-started.md): Any Airbyte Cloud environment can upgrade to Enterprise Flex. To learn more about upgrading, talk to sales.

#### multi-region

Self-Managed Enterprise customers can use Airbyte's public API to define regions and create independent data planes that operate in those regions. This ensures you're satisfying your data residency and governance requirements with a single Airbyte deployment, and it can help you reduce data egress costs with cloud providers.

- [Multiple region deployments (Self-Managed Enterprise)](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/enterprise-setup/multi-region.md): Self-Managed Enterprise customers can use Airbyte's public API to define regions and create independent data planes that operate in those regions. This ensures you're satisfying your data residency and governance requirements with a single Airbyte deployment, and it can help you reduce data egress costs with cloud providers.

### managing-airbyte


#### connector-updates

While maintaining an Airbyte instance, you'll need to manage connector updates. These are essential for improved functionality, reliability, and compatibility over time. Our team and community contributors are dedicated to maintaining up-to-date connectors. Reasons for updates can be broadly categorized into bug fixes, new features, and changes that impact the user experience or the functionality of the connector.
