Reasons for updates can be broadly categorized into bug fixes, new features, and changes that impact the user experience or the functionality of the connector.

### move-data

In Airbyte, you move data from sources to destinations using connectors. These connectors form connections. Connections contain streams of data and they're responsible for syncing your data.

- [Moving data](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/move-data.md): In Airbyte, you move data from sources to destinations using connectors. These connectors form connections. Connections contain streams of data and they're responsible for syncing your data.

#### add-connection

After you add a source and a destination, add a new connection to start syncing data from your source to your destination.

- [Add a connection](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/move-data/add-connection.md): After you add a source and a destination, add a new connection to start syncing data from your source to your destination.

#### elt-data-activation

Data activation enables you to move data out of your data warehouse and into the operational tools where work happens, like CRMs, marketing platforms, and support systems. With this capability, you can deliver modeled data directly to points of action and systems people already use, helping your organization respond faster and more effectively.

- [Data activation (reverse ETL)](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/move-data/elt-data-activation.md): Data activation enables you to move data out of your data warehouse and into the operational tools where work happens, like CRMs, marketing platforms, and support systems. With this capability, you can deliver modeled data directly to points of action and systems people already use, helping your organization respond faster and more effectively.

#### rejected-records

When syncing data to a data activation destination, you may encounter rejected records. Rejected records are records Airbyte was unable to sync to your destination, even though the sync itself was otherwise successful.

- [Rejected records](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/move-data/rejected-records.md): When syncing data to a data activation destination, you may encounter rejected records. Rejected records are records Airbyte was unable to sync to your destination, even though the sync itself was otherwise successful.

### operating-airbyte


#### external-secrets

This guide provides step-by-step instructions for configuring external secrets management with Airbyte. External secrets management allows Airbyte to securely store and manage connection credentials in your cloud provider's secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, or Google Cloud Secret Manager) instead of storing them in Airbyte's internal database.

- [External Secret Management](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operating-airbyte/external-secrets.md): This guide provides step-by-step instructions for configuring external secrets management with Airbyte. External secrets management allows Airbyte to securely store and manage connection credentials in your cloud provider's secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, or Google Cloud Secret Manager) instead of storing them in Airbyte's internal database.

#### ip-allowlist

Airbyte Cloud runs and syncs your data using a specific set of IP addresses. Allow these IPs in your firewall to ensure Airbyte users can correctly use the platform.

- [IP allow list for Cloud](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operating-airbyte/ip-allowlist.md): Airbyte Cloud runs and syncs your data using a specific set of IP addresses. Allow these IPs in your firewall to ensure Airbyte users can correctly use the platform.

#### privatelink

Private Links allow Airbyte Cloud to securely connect to your data sources and destinations without using the public internet or exposing IPs. Traffic between Airbyte and your resources stays entirely within your cloud provider's private network, providing enhanced security for organizations with strict network isolation requirements.

- [Private Links](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operating-airbyte/privatelink.md): Private Links allow Airbyte Cloud to securely connect to your data sources and destinations without using the public internet or exposing IPs. Traffic between Airbyte and your resources stays entirely within your cloud provider's private network, providing enhanced security for organizations with strict network isolation requirements.

#### security

Airbyte is committed to keeping your data safe by following industry-standard practices for securing physical deployments, setting access policies, and leveraging the security features of leading Cloud providers.

- [Security](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operating-airbyte/security.md): Airbyte is committed to keeping your data safe by following industry-standard practices for securing physical deployments, setting access policies, and leveraging the security features of leading Cloud providers.

### operator-guides


#### browsing-output-logs

Airbyte records the full logs as a part of each sync. These logs can be used to understand the underlying operations Airbyte performs to read data from the source and write to the destination as a part of the Airbyte Protocol. The logs includes many details, including any errors that can be helpful when troubleshooting sync errors.

- [Browsing logs](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operator-guides/browsing-output-logs.md): Airbyte records the full logs as a part of each sync. The logs includes many details, including any errors that can be helpful when troubleshooting sync errors.

#### clear

As of Airbyte v1.0.0, the term "Clear" has replaced "Reset" in the Airbyte UI and documentation. The functionality described on this page is the new "Clear" functionality. Prior to Airbyte 1.0, "Reset" was used to describe similar functionality, including a mandatory re-sync of the data, which has been removed.

- [Clearing your data](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/operator-guides/clear.md): As of Airbyte v1.0.0, the term "Clear" has replaced "Reset" in the Airbyte UI and documentation. ### organizations-workspaces

Organizations and workspaces are the highest levels of structure in Airbyte. They're the primary ways you segregate data and connections, manage access, and control billing.

- [Organizations and workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/organizations-workspaces.md): Organizations and workspaces are the highest levels of structure in Airbyte. They're the primary ways you segregate data and connections, manage access, and control billing.

#### organizations

The highest level of structure in Airbyte is an organization. Organizations are how you manage membership and permissions, billing (if applicable), and overall account usage.

- [Organizations](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/organizations-workspaces/organizations.md): The highest level of structure in Airbyte is an organization. Organizations are how you manage membership and permissions, billing (if applicable), and overall account usage.

#### workspaces

Each organization consists of one or more workspaces. A workspace groups sources, destinations, and connections. You can also use workspaces to assign access and permissions. You can use a single workspace for everything, or you can divide your organization into multiple workspaces.

- [Workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/organizations-workspaces/workspaces.md): Each organization consists of one or more workspaces. #### jobs

In Airbyte, all connector operations are run as 'workloads' — a pod encapsulating the discrete invocation of one or more connectors' interface method(s) (READ, WRITE, CHECK, DISCOVER, SPEC).

- [Workloads & Jobs](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/understanding-airbyte/jobs.md): In Airbyte, all connector operations are run as 'workloads' — a pod encapsulating the discrete invocation of one or more connectors' interface method(s) (READ, WRITE, CHECK, DISCOVER, SPEC).

#### json-avro-conversion

When an Airbyte data stream is synced to the Avro or Parquet format (e.g. Parquet on S3), the source JSON schema is converted to an Avro schema, then the JSON object is converted to an Avro record based on the Avro schema (and further to Parquet if necessary). Because the data stream can come from any data source, the JSON to Avro conversion process has the following rules and limitations.

- [JSON to Avro Conversion for Blob Storage Destinations](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/understanding-airbyte/json-avro-conversion.md): When an Airbyte data stream is synced to the Avro or Parquet format (e.g. Parquet on S3), the source JSON schema is converted to an Avro schema, then the JSON object is converted to an Avro record based on the Avro schema (and further to Parquet if necessary). Because the data stream can come from any data source, the JSON to Avro conversion process has the following rules and limitations.

### using-airbyte


#### configuring-api-access

Most programmatic interactions with Airbyte require an access token. An access token represents an individual Airbyte user, and it has the same permissions as that Airbyte user.

- [Get an API access token](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/configuring-api-access.md): Most programmatic interactions with Airbyte require an access token. An access token represents an individual Airbyte user, and it has the same permissions as that Airbyte user.

#### configuring-schema

A connection's schema typically consists of one or many streams. Each stream is most commonly associated with a database table or an API endpoint. Within a stream, there are typically several fields or columns. You can sync specific data from your sources by selecting which stream or fields.

- [Configuring schemas](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/configuring-schema.md): A connection's schema typically consists of one or many streams. Each stream is most commonly associated with a database table or an API endpoint. Within a stream, there are typically several fields or columns. You can sync specific data from your sources by selecting which stream or fields.

#### core-concepts

Airbyte enables you to build data pipelines and replicate data from a source to a destination. You can configure how frequently the data is synced, what data is replicated, and how the data is written to in the destination.

- [Core Concepts](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts.md): Airbyte enables you to build data pipelines and replicate data from a source to a destination. You can configure how frequently the data is synced, what data is replicated, and how the data is written to in the destination.

##### direct-load-tables

Direct loading is an improvement to Typing and Deduping. Airbyte intends to eventually replace typing and deduping with direct-load. Under direct-load, the final tables in your destination are identical to their typed and deduped version, but without the need to store the raw tables in your destination.

- [Direct loading tables](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/direct-load-tables.md): Direct loading is an improvement to Typing and Deduping. Airbyte intends to eventually replace typing and deduping with direct-load. Under direct-load, the final tables in your destination are identical to their typed and deduped version, but without the need to store the raw tables in your destination.

##### namespaces

Namespaces are used to generally organize data, separate tests and production data, and enforce permissions. In most cases, namespaces are schemas in the database you're replicating to.

- [Namespaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/namespaces.md): Namespaces are used to generally organize data, separate tests and production data, and enforce permissions. In most cases, namespaces are schemas in the database you're replicating to.

##### sync-modes

A sync mode governs how Airbyte reads from a source and writes to a destination. Airbyte provides different sync modes to account for various use cases. To minimize confusion, a mode's behavior is reflected in its name. The easiest way to understand Airbyte's sync modes is to understand how the modes are named.

- [Sync Modes](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes.md): A sync mode governs how Airbyte reads from a source and writes to a destination. Airbyte provides different sync modes to account for various use cases. To minimize confusion, a mode's behavior is reflected in its name. The easiest way to understand Airbyte's sync modes is to understand how the modes are named.
- [Full Refresh - Append](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes/full-refresh-append.md): The Full Refresh modes are the simplest methods that Airbyte uses to sync data, as they always retrieve all available data requested from the source, regardless of whether it has been synced before. This contrasts with Incremental sync, which does not sync data that has already been synced before.
- [Full Refresh - Overwrite](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes/full-refresh-overwrite.md): The Full Refresh modes are the simplest methods that Airbyte uses to sync data, as they always retrieve all available information requested from the source, regardless of whether it has been synced before. This contrasts with Incremental sync, which does not sync data that has already been synced before.
- [Full Refresh - Overwrite + Deduped](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes/full-refresh-overwrite-deduped.md): The Full Refresh modes are the simplest methods that Airbyte uses to sync data, as they always retrieve all available information requested from the source, regardless of whether it has been synced before. This contrasts with Incremental sync, which does not sync data that has already been synced before.
- [Incremental Sync - Append](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes/incremental-append.md): Airbyte supports syncing data in Incremental | Append mode, which syncs only replicate new or modified data. This prevents re-fetching data that you have already replicated from a source. If the sync is running for the first time, it is equivalent to a Full Refresh since all data will be considered as new.
- [Incremental Sync - Append + Deduped](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/core-concepts/sync-modes/incremental-append-deduped.md): This sync mode syncs data incrementally, which means that only new or modified data will be synced. In contrast with the Incremental Append mode, this mode updates rows that have been modified instead of adding a new version of the row with the updated data.

#### mappings

Use mappings to hash, encrypt, and rename fields, and filter rows. You set up mappings on each stream, ensuring your source data arrives in your destination exactly as you want it.

- [Mappings](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/mappings.md): Use mappings to hash, encrypt, and rename fields, and filter rows. You set up mappings on each stream, ensuring your source data arrives in your destination exactly as you want it.

#### schema-change-management

You can specify for each connection how Airbyte should handle any change of schema in the source. This process helps ensure accurate and efficient data syncs, minimizing errors and saving you time and effort in managing your data pipelines.

- [Schema change  management](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/schema-change-management.md): You can specify for each connection how Airbyte should handle any change of schema in the source. This process helps ensure accurate and efficient data syncs, minimizing errors and saving you time and effort in managing your data pipelines.

#### sync-files-and-records

Airbyte supports moving files and records together in the same connection. Some sources are a mix of structured data and unstructured attachments. The combination of structured and unstructured data drives more robust knowledge systems with more context, something critical to successful AI systems.

- [Sync files and records together](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/sync-files-and-records.md): Airbyte supports moving files and records together in the same connection. Some sources are a mix of structured data and unstructured attachments. The combination of structured and unstructured data drives more robust knowledge systems with more context, something critical to successful AI systems.

#### tagging

As time goes on, the number of connections in your workspace tends to increase. Use tags to organize connections based on any set of criteria you like, then filter your connections based on the tags you want to see.

- [Tagging connections](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/tagging.md): As time goes on, the number of connections in your workspace tends to increase. Use tags to organize connections based on any set of criteria you like, then filter your connections based on the tags you want to see.

#### workspaces

You can create, manage, and delete workspaces, and control access to them.

- [Manage workspaces](https://docs.airbyte.io/platform/using-airbyte/workspaces.md): You can create, manage, and delete workspaces, and control access to them.
